docs.title: bdbvsubmission
docs.text:
The gated weekly submission to the BDBV Modeling Hub, from fitting candidates to the hub pull request.

bdbvsubmission is the package in packages/bdbvsubmission of the repository (Packages). It checks each candidate forecast, falls back along a chain of models when one fails, and records what it submitted. It uses the standard library only.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
It has its own environment and lock, so the submission runs with exactly what it needs. It is not in the root workspace, so uv sync at the root does not install it.

uv pip install "git+https://github.com/seabbs/bdbv-hub-modelling#subdirectory=packages/bdbvsubmission"

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
Each round has a reference date, a Saturday. Its submission window opens six days before, at midnight in Kinshasa, and closes three days before.

import datetime as dt

from bdbvsubmission.window import KINSHASA, window_for

win = window_for(dt.date(2026, 11, 21))
assert win.opens == dt.datetime(2026, 11, 15, tzinfo=KINSHASA)
assert win.closes == dt.datetime(2026, 11, 18, tzinfo=KINSHASA)
assert win.is_open(dt.datetime(2026, 11, 16, 12, tzinfo=KINSHASA))

A candidate's hub file holds sample trajectories. We write a small one with two samples for one province and two weeks. One value is negative.

import csv
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from bdbvsubmission.hubdata import TARGET, read_samples

path = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "candidate.csv"
with path.open("w", newline="") as fh:
    out = csv.writer(fh)
    out.writerow(
        [
            "reference_date",
            "forecast_date",
            "target",
            "target_end_date",
            "location",
            "output_type",
            "output_type_id",
            "value",
        ]
    )
    for sample, values in (("1", (4, 6)), ("2", (5, -1))):
        for week, value in zip(("2026-11-14", "2026-11-21"), values):
            out.writerow(
                [
                    "2026-11-21",
                    "2026-11-17",
                    TARGET,
                    week,
                    "CD-NK",
                    "sample",
                    sample,
                    value,
                ]
            )
samples = read_samples(path)
assert samples.locations == ["CD-NK"]
assert samples.week_values("CD-NK", "2026-11-21") == [6.0, -1.0]

Each check returns pass, warn, fail or skip. The negative value fails check_values, and a failure blocks the candidate.

from bdbvsubmission.check_forecast import check_samples, check_values
from bdbvsubmission.common import blocks, worst

checks = [check_values(samples), check_samples(samples, n=2)]
assert [c.status for c in checks] == ["fail", "pass"]
assert checks[0].locations == ["CD-NK"]
assert blocks(worst(c.status for c in checks))

The failure names one province. The gate then keeps the candidate and takes that province from the next candidate in the chain (bdbvsubmission.location_fallback).

docs.title: Read the fallback chain
docs.text:
policy.toml lists the candidates in the order the gate tries them, and the thresholds of each check. We write a short policy with one renewal model and the random walk.

from bdbvsubmission.policy import fit_timeout, load_policy

policy_file = path.parent / "policy.toml"
policy_file.write_text(
    """
[timing]
fit_cap_minutes = 350
reserve_minutes = 45
min_fit_minutes = 30

[[candidates]]
id = "main"
kind = "main"
config = "main"
model = "renewal"
stage = "primary"
label = "zone renewal model"

[[candidates]]
id = "randomwalk"
kind = "randomwalk"
config = "randomwalk"
stage = "baseline"
label = "random walk baseline"

[convergence.fail]
rhat = 1.1
ess_bulk = 25
ess_tail = 25
divergent_fraction = 0.05

[convergence.warn]
rhat = 1.05
ess_bulk = 100
ess_tail = 100
divergent_fraction = 0.01

[ppc]
stream = "total"

[checks]
samples = 100
"""
)
policy = load_policy(policy_file)
assert [c.id for c in policy.chain()] == ["main", "randomwalk"]

A fit's timeout is the job cap, less the time kept free for the gate before the window closes.

assert fit_timeout(policy, None) == 350
assert fit_timeout(policy, minutes_left=120) == 75
assert fit_timeout(policy, minutes_left=50) == 30

docs.title: Gate a fit on its convergence
docs.text:
verdict compares a fit's headline diagnostics with the policy's thresholds. Past a fail threshold the fit is ruled out and the chain moves on. Past a warn threshold it is reported only.

from bdbvsubmission.summarise_fit import verdict

head = {
    "max_rhat": 1.07,
    "min_ess_bulk": 400.0,
    "min_ess_tail": 300.0,
    "divergent_fraction": 0.0,
}
status, failures, warnings = verdict(head, policy.convergence)
assert status == "warn"
assert failures == []
assert len(warnings) == 1

docs.title: bdbvsubmission.window
docs.text:
The hub's submission window, in Kinshasa time.

hub-config/tasks.json sets submissions_due to -6 to -4 days relative to the reference_date (a Saturday), in the hub's timezone (Africa/Kinshasa, from admin.json). That is Sunday 00:00 to Tuesday 23:59 of the reference week. Kinshasa is UTC+1 with no daylight saving, so a fixed offset is exact and needs no tz database on the runner.

class Window:
    """One round's submission window."""

    reference_date: dt.date
    opens: dt.datetime
    closes: dt.datetime  # exclusive

    def is_open(self, now: dt.datetime) -> bool:
        """Whether `now` falls inside the window."""
        return self.opens <= now < self.closes

    def hours_left(self, now: dt.datetime) -> float:
        """Hours until the window closes (negative once closed)."""
        return (self.closes - now).total_seconds() / 3600

def window_for(reference_date: dt.date) -> Window:
    """Return the window of the round with this reference date."""
    if reference_date.weekday() != SATURDAY:
        raise ValueError(f"{reference_date} is not a Saturday")
    opens = dt.datetime.combine(
        reference_date - dt.timedelta(days=6), dt.time(), KINSHASA
    )
    closes = dt.datetime.combine(
        reference_date - dt.timedelta(days=3), dt.time(), KINSHASA
    )
    return Window(reference_date, opens, closes)

def current_window(now: dt.datetime) -> Window:
    """Return the window open at `now`, or the next one to open."""
    local = now.astimezone(KINSHASA).date()
    ref = local + dt.timedelta(days=(SATURDAY - local.weekday()) % 7)
    win = window_for(ref)
    if now >= win.closes:
        win = window_for(ref + dt.timedelta(days=7))
    return win

def minutes_left(
    reference_date: str, now: dt.datetime, *, ignore_window: bool = False
) -> float | None:
    """Minutes until the round's window closes, or None without a limit.

    There is no limit when no round is given or the window is ignored
    (dry runs on past rounds).
    """
    if not reference_date or ignore_window:
        return None
    win = window_for(dt.date.fromisoformat(reference_date))
    return (win.closes - now).total_seconds() / 60

def parse_now(value: str | None) -> dt.datetime:
    """Parse an ISO timestamp, defaulting to the current UTC time."""
    if not value:
        return dt.datetime.now(dt.UTC)
    parsed = dt.datetime.fromisoformat(value)
    if parsed.tzinfo is None:
        parsed = parsed.replace(tzinfo=dt.UTC)
    return parsed

docs.title: bdbvsubmission.policy
docs.text:
The fallback chain and the thresholds, read from policy.toml.

The chain is an ordered list of candidates, and the first that clears every check is submitted. It runs through the renewal models from the most to the least complex, then randomwalknowcast (random walk on a nowcast) and randomwalk (the random walk baseline, built from the data alone). There are no refits.

Stage primary candidates are fitted models, read from the fit store (bdbvhub fit-store unpack). Stage baseline candidates need no fit.

The wait for the store's fits stops reserve_minutes before the window closes for the gate and the pull request, so the chain can always reach the fallback or random walk in time.

KINDS = ('main', 'fallback', 'randomwalk', 'shadow', 'direct')

A shadow candidate is fitted and checked with its stage but is never part of the chain, so it is never submitted. It lets a variant run weekly before it is chosen. A direct candidate is a hub model of its own, run in its job with no fit and never in another model's chain.

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Policy:
    """The parsed policy file."""

    candidates: list[Candidate]
    convergence: dict[str, dict[str, float]]
    checks: dict[str, Any]
    ppc: dict[str, Any]
    timing: Timing
    own: bool = False
    """A hub model of its own (`for_model` with `only`), whose chain may
    be a `direct` candidate."""

    def chain(self) -> list[Candidate]:
        """Candidates in submission order.

        `direct` candidates are in no chain but their own.
        """
        return [
            c
            for c in self.candidates
            if c.kind != "shadow" and (self.own or c.kind != "direct")
        ]

    def stage(self, name: str) -> list[Candidate]:
        """Candidates fitted in one stage, shadows included."""
        shadows = [c for c in self.candidates if c.kind == "shadow"]
        return [c for c in [*self.chain(), *shadows] if c.stage == name]

    def for_model(self, model: str, only: bool = False) -> Policy:
        """The chain from the candidate of `model` on.

        Candidates before it are still fitted and checked, as shadows.
        A model with no candidate keeps the
        policy as it is.

        With `only`, the chain is that candidate alone, for a hub model
        that must never be submitted as anything else. The others are
        still built as shadows, as references for the checks, and are
        never selected. Without it, `direct` candidates are left out.
        """
        pool = (
            self.candidates
            if only
            else [c for c in self.candidates if c.kind != "direct"]
        )
        chain = replace(self, candidates=pool, own=only).chain()
        names = [c.model or c.id for c in chain]
        if model not in names:
            if only:
                raise ValueError(f"{model!r} has no candidate")
            return replace(self, candidates=pool)
        start = names.index(model)
        kept = {c.id for c in chain[start : start + 1 if only else None]}
        cands = [c if c.id in kept else replace(c, kind="shadow") for c in pool]
        return replace(self, candidates=cands, own=only)

    def get(self, cid: str) -> Candidate:
        """Look up a candidate by id."""
        for c in self.candidates:
            if c.id == cid:
                return c
        raise KeyError(cid)

def load_policy(path: Path | str) -> Policy:
    """Read and check `policy.toml`."""
    raw = tomllib.loads(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    cands = []
    for c in raw["candidates"]:
        cand = Candidate(
            id=c["id"],
            kind=c["kind"],
            config=c["config"],
            stage=c["stage"],
            label=c["label"],
            sampler=dict(c.get("sampler", {})),
            model=c.get("model", ""),
        )
        if cand.kind not in KINDS:
            raise ValueError(f"candidate {cand.id}: unknown kind {cand.kind}")
        if cand.stage not in STAGES:
            raise ValueError(f"candidate {cand.id}: unknown stage {cand.stage}")
        cands.append(cand)
    ids = [c.id for c in cands]
    if len(set(ids)) != len(ids):
        raise ValueError("candidate ids must be unique")
    if not cands or cands[0].kind != "main":
        raise ValueError("the first candidate must be the main model")
    return Policy(
        candidates=cands,
        convergence=raw["convergence"],
        checks=raw["checks"],
        ppc=raw["ppc"],
        timing=Timing(**{k: int(v) for k, v in raw["timing"].items()}),
    )

How long to wait for, or make, a fit: the cap, less the gate's time.

def fit_timeout(policy: Policy, minutes_left: float | None) -> int:
    """How long to wait for, or make, a fit: the cap, less the gate's time.

    `minutes_left` is the time to the window's close (None for no
    limit). The timeout never drops below `min_fit_minutes`; a fit that
    cannot finish then fails and the chain moves on.
    """
    t = policy.timing
    if minutes_left is None:
        return t.fit_cap_minutes
    room = int(minutes_left) - t.reserve_minutes
    return max(t.min_fit_minutes, min(t.fit_cap_minutes, room))

def main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
    """Print the matrix for a stage and set it as a step output."""
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    p.add_argument("--policy", type=Path, required=True)
    p.add_argument("--stage", choices=STAGES, required=True)
    p.add_argument("--only", nargs="*", default=None)
    p.add_argument(
        "--model",
        default="",
        help="The chosen model; random walk makes a randomwalk-only chain",
    )
    p.add_argument(
        "--only-model",
        action="store_true",
        help="A chain of --model alone, with the others as shadows",
    )
    add_deadline_args(p)
    args = p.parse_args(argv)
    entries = matrix(
        load_policy(args.policy).for_model(args.model, args.only_model),
        args.stage,
        deadline_minutes(args),
    )
    if args.only is not None:
        entries = [e for e in entries if e["id"] in args.only]
    text = json.dumps({"include": entries})
    set_outputs({"matrix": text, "count": len(entries)})
    print(text)
    return 0

docs.title: bdbvsubmission.tracks
docs.text:
Which hub models a run submits, from packages/bdbvhub/config/hub.toml.

Each hub model is opted in on its own with submit = true. DRY_RUN stays the global switch: an opted-in model in a dry run builds and checks everything but pushes nothing.

  • renewal ([submission]): the renewal chain, from model there, which may fall back down the chain in packages/bdbvsubmission/policy.toml.
  • baseline ([models.randomwalknowcast]): random walk on a nowcast. It has no fallback. If it cannot run, its round is skipped and nothing is submitted under its id.
  • foundation_zeroshot ([models.foundation]): fine-tuned Chronos-2, run in its own job, with no fallback either.

def load_tracks(path: Path | str) -> list[Track]:
    """Read the hub models and decide which run."""
    with Path(path).open("rb") as fh:
        cfg = tomllib.load(fh)
    sub = cfg["submission"]
    tracks = [_track(sub["model_abbr"], sub["model"], bool(sub.get("submit")))]
    for model, entry in cfg.get("models", {}).items():
        tracks.append(
            _track(entry["model_abbr"], model, bool(entry.get("submit")))
        )
    return tracks

docs.title: bdbvsubmission.detect_new_vintage
docs.text:
Decide whether this scheduled run should forecast and submit.

The hub publishes a new data vintage by committing to target-data/ and auxiliary-data/, usually between Friday and Monday. This compares the newest commit touching those paths, and the newest as_of in time-series.csv, with the ledger of what earlier runs used. The ledger (state.json) lives on the submission-ledger branch of this repo.

Rules, for the round whose window is open now:

  • The round must be open in the hub's tasks.json.
  • Submit once per round: a round the ledger records as submitted (its hub PR exists) is left alone, unless the model code on main changed since the commit it was submitted from (CODE_PATHS). Then the run updates the round's PR. A manual dispatch can always resubmit.
  • Run when the hub data changed since this round last ran (a new round, or a data fix during the window, which updates the round's PR).
  • On a new round, only run on fresh data: an as_of no earlier round used. Last week's data are not resubmitted on Sunday morning, but if nothing new lands by the last stale_fallback_hours of the window the round runs on what there is rather than being missed. With a check every 3 hours, that is the first check in the last day of the window.
  • force (manual dispatch) skips the data checks but never the window, unless ignore_window is also set, which only a dry run may use.

Subcommands: detect writes the decision to $GITHUB_OUTPUT; record updates the ledger after a run, and record-model records each hub model's submission in the round under models.

class GhHubSource:
    """Read the hub through `gh api` and raw.githubusercontent.com."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        repo: str = HUB,
        paths: Sequence[str] = WATCHED,
        runner: Runner = subprocess_runner,
    ) -> None:
        self.repo, self.paths, self.runner = repo, paths, runner

    def _api(self, endpoint: str) -> Any:
        out = self.runner(["gh", "api", endpoint]).stdout
        return json.loads(out)

    def _raw(self, ref: str, path: str) -> str:
        url = f"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/{self.repo}/{ref}/{path}"
        with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=120) as resp:
            return str(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))

    def data_version(self) -> DataVersion:
        """Return the newest data commit, `main` HEAD and latest `as_of`."""
        head = self._api(f"repos/{self.repo}/commits/main")["sha"]
        newest = ("", "")
        for path in self.paths:
            commits = self._api(
                f"repos/{self.repo}/commits?sha={head}&path={path}&per_page=1"
            )
            if commits:
                c = commits[0]
                stamp = c["commit"]["committer"]["date"]
                newest = max(newest, (stamp, c["sha"]))
        if not newest[1]:
            raise RuntimeError("no commits found for the watched hub paths")
        text = self._raw(head, "target-data/time-series.csv")
        return DataVersion(
            data_commit=newest[1],
            committed_at=newest[0],
            hub_ref=head,
            as_of=max_as_of(io.StringIO(text)),
        )

    def tasks(self, ref: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Return `tasks.json` at `ref`."""
        data: dict[str, Any] = json.loads(
            self._raw(ref, "hub-config/tasks.json")
        )
        return data

def open_reference_dates(
    tasks: Mapping[str, Any], target: str = TARGET
) -> set[str]:
    """Reference dates accepted by the round that takes `target`."""
    out: set[str] = set()
    for rnd in tasks.get("rounds", []):
        for mt in rnd.get("model_tasks", []):
            ids = mt.get("task_ids", {})
            t = ids.get("target", {})
            targets = (t.get("required") or []) + (t.get("optional") or [])
            if target not in targets:
                continue
            r = ids.get("reference_date", {})
            out.update((r.get("required") or []) + (r.get("optional") or []))
    return out

def decide(
    state: dict[str, Any],
    version: DataVersion,
    tasks: dict[str, Any],
    now: dt.datetime,
    *,
    force: bool = False,
    ignore_window: bool = False,
    reference_date: str | None = None,
    stale_fallback_hours: float = 24.0,
    changed_since: Callable[[str], bool] = code_changed,
) -> Decision:
    """Apply the run rules in the module docstring.

    `changed_since` says whether the model code changed since a commit.
    """
    win = (
        window_for(dt.date.fromisoformat(reference_date))
        if reference_date
        else current_window(now)
    )
    ref = win.reference_date.isoformat()
    rounds: dict[str, Any] = state.get("rounds", {})
    entry = rounds.get(ref)
    new_for_round = entry is None or entry.get("data_commit") != (
        version.data_commit
    )
    earlier_as_of = {
        r.get("as_of") for k, r in rounds.items() if k < ref and r.get("as_of")
    }
    earlier_commits = {
        r.get("data_commit") for k, r in rounds.items() if k < ref
    }
    fresh = (
        version.as_of not in earlier_as_of
        if version.as_of
        else version.data_commit not in earlier_commits
    )
    submitted = entry is not None and entry.get("status") == "submitted"
    code_commit = (entry or {}).get("code_commit", "")
    code = submitted and bool(code_commit) and changed_since(code_commit)
    window_open = win.is_open(now)
    hours_left = round(win.hours_left(now), 2)
    round_open = ref in open_reference_dates(tasks)

    def out(run: bool, reason: str) -> Decision:
        return Decision(
            should_run=run,
            reason=reason,
            reference_date=ref,
            window_open=window_open,
            hours_left=hours_left,
            round_open=round_open,
            new_for_round=new_for_round,
            fresh=fresh,
            code_changed=code,
            data_commit=version.data_commit,
            hub_ref=version.hub_ref,
            as_of=version.as_of,
        )

    if not window_open and not ignore_window:
        return out(False, f"the window for {ref} is not open")
    if not round_open and not ignore_window:
        return out(False, f"{ref} is not an open round in the hub's tasks.json")
    if force:
        return out(True, "forced by manual dispatch")
    if code:
        return out(True, f"model code changed since {ref} was submitted")
    if submitted:
        return out(False, f"{ref} already has a hub PR")
    if not new_for_round:
        return out(False, f"no new hub data since {ref} last ran")
    if entry is not None:
        return out(True, "hub data changed during the window; updating")
    if fresh:
        return out(True, f"new data vintage {version.as_of or '?'}")
    if window_open and hours_left <= stale_fallback_hours:
        return out(
            True,
            f"no new vintage and {hours_left:.1f} h left; "
            "submitting on the latest data",
        )
    return out(False, "waiting for a new data vintage")

    entry["history"] = history
    entry["models"] = new["rounds"].get(reference_date, {}).get("models", {})
    new["rounds"][reference_date] = entry

def main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
    """Command line entry point."""
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    sub = p.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)

    det.add_argument("--state", type=Path, required=True)
    det.add_argument("--hub", default=HUB)

    det.add_argument("--now", default=None)

    det.add_argument("--reference-date", default=None)
    det.add_argument("--stale-fallback-hours", type=float, default=24.0)
    det.add_argument("--out", type=Path, default=None)
    rec = sub.add_parser("record")
    rec.add_argument("--state", type=Path, required=True)
    rec.add_argument("--reference-date", required=True)
    rec.add_argument("--data-commit", required=True)
    rec.add_argument("--as-of", default="")
    rec.add_argument("--status", required=True)
    rec.add_argument("--produced-by", default="")
    rec.add_argument("--pr-url", default="")
    rec.add_argument("--run", default="")
    rec.add_argument("--code-commit", default="")
    mod = sub.add_parser("record-model")
    mod.add_argument("--state", type=Path, required=True)
    mod.add_argument("--reference-date", required=True)
    mod.add_argument("--model-id", required=True)
    mod.add_argument("--status", required=True)
    mod.add_argument("--archive", required=True)
    mod.add_argument("--produced-by", default="")
    mod.add_argument("--pr-url", default="")
    mod.add_argument("--run", default="")
    mod.add_argument("--code-commit", default="")
    args = p.parse_args(argv)

    state = read_json(args.state) if args.state.exists() else empty_state()
    if args.cmd == "record":
        write_json(
            args.state,
            record(
                state,
                args.reference_date,
                data_commit=args.data_commit,
                as_of=args.as_of,
                status=args.status,
                produced_by=args.produced_by,
                pr_url=args.pr_url,
                run=args.run,
                code_commit=args.code_commit,
            ),
        )
        return 0
    if args.cmd == "record-model":
        write_json(
            args.state,
            record_model(
                state,
                args.reference_date,
                args.model_id,
                status=args.status,
                archive=args.archive,
                produced_by=args.produced_by,
                pr_url=args.pr_url,
                run=args.run,
                code_commit=args.code_commit,
            ),
        )
        return 0

    if args.ignore_window and not args.force:
        p.error("--ignore-window needs --force")
    source: HubSource = (
        FixtureHubSource(args.fixture)
        if args.fixture
        else GhHubSource(args.hub)
    )
    version = source.data_version()
    decision = decide(
        state,
        version,
        source.tasks(version.hub_ref),
        parse_now(args.now),
        force=args.force,
        ignore_window=args.ignore_window,
        reference_date=args.reference_date,
        stale_fallback_hours=args.stale_fallback_hours,
    )
    set_outputs(asdict(decision))
    append_summary(_summary(decision))
    if args.out:
        write_json(args.out, asdict(decision))
    print(json.dumps(asdict(decision), indent=2), file=sys.stdout)
    return 0

def read_samples(path: Path | str, latest: bool = True) -> Samples:
    """Read a hub-format sample CSV.

    Count rows are sample trajectories (`values`); `RT_TARGET` rows are
    kept apart in `rt`, so the count checks never see them.

    A resubmitted file holds several forecasts, one per `forecast_date`.
    With `latest` only the newest is read, which is the one this run adds.
    Every date is still listed in `forecast_dates`.
    """
    with Path(path).open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        reader = csv.DictReader(fh)
        out = Samples(columns=list(reader.fieldnames or []), rows=0)
        table = list(reader)
        out.forecast_dates = {r.get("forecast_date", "") for r in table}
        newest = max(out.forecast_dates, default="")
        for line, row in enumerate(table, start=2):
            if latest and row.get("forecast_date", "") != newest:
                continue
            out.rows += 1
            out.reference_dates.add(row.get("reference_date", ""))
            out.targets.add(row.get("target", ""))
            try:
                value = float(row.get("value", ""))
            except ValueError:
                out.unparsable.append(f"line {line}: {row.get('value')!r}")
                value = math.nan
            if row.get("target") == RT_TARGET:
                out.rt_output_types.add(row.get("output_type", ""))
                levels = out.rt[row.get("location", "")][
                    row.get("target_end_date", "")
                ]
                level = row.get("output_type_id", "")
                if level in levels:
                    out.duplicates += 1
                levels[level] = value
                continue
            out.output_types.add(row.get("output_type", ""))
            traj = out.values[row.get("location", "")][
                row.get("output_type_id", "")
            ]
            week = row.get("target_end_date", "")
            if week in traj:
                out.duplicates += 1
            traj[week] = value
    return out

def quantile(values: list[float], q: float) -> float:
    """Linear-interpolation quantile of a list (NaN when empty)."""
    clean = sorted(v for v in values if not math.isnan(v))
    if not clean:
        return math.nan
    pos = q * (len(clean) - 1)
    lo = math.floor(pos)
    hi = min(lo + 1, len(clean) - 1)
    return clean[lo] + (clean[hi] - clean[lo]) * (pos - lo)

Source code in packages/bdbvsubmission/src/bdbvsubmission/forecast_date.py 
def problems(
    cols: list[str],
    rows: list[Row],
    previous: tuple[list[str], list[Row]] | None = None,
    today: dt.date | None = None,
) -> list[str]:
    """List why a file would fail the hub's `forecast_date` checks.

    Without `previous` every row is new. With a `today`, the new date must
    be within a day of it. The hub stops at its first failure, so this
    returns at most one message.
    """
    if cols.count(FORECAST_DATE) != 1:
        return [f"`{FORECAST_DATE}` must be a column, exactly once"]
    dates = [r.get(FORECAST_DATE, "") for r in rows]
    for i, value in enumerate(dates):
        if parse_date(value) is None:
            return [
                f"`{FORECAST_DATE}` must be a nonblank YYYY-MM-DD date; "
                f'CSV line {i + 2} has "{value}"'
            ]
    for i, r in enumerate(rows):
        ref = r.get("reference_date", "")
        if parse_date(ref) is None:
            return [f'`reference_date` "{ref}" is not a YYYY-MM-DD date']
        if dates[i] > ref:
            return [
                f"`{FORECAST_DATE}` must be on or before `reference_date`; "
                f"CSV line {i + 2} has {dates[i]} after {ref}"
            ]
    order = sorted(cols)
    if previous is None:
        new = dates
    else:
        pcols, prows = previous
        if FORECAST_DATE not in pcols:
            return [
                "the hub's copy has no `forecast_date` column, so it "
                "cannot be appended to"
            ]
        if sorted(pcols) != order:
            return ["the appended file must keep the existing columns"]
        old = {r[FORECAST_DATE] for r in prows}
        kept = Counter(
            tuple(r[c] for c in order) for r in rows if r[FORECAST_DATE] in old
        )
        if kept != Counter(tuple(r[c] for c in order) for r in prows):
            return [
                "every existing row must be kept unchanged, duplicates "
                "included, and new rows need a new `forecast_date`"
            ]
        new = [d for d in dates if d not in old]
    distinct = sorted(set(new))
    if len(distinct) != 1:
        return [
            "a submission must add exactly one new `forecast_date`, "
            f"found {distinct or 'none'}"
        ]
    if today is not None:
        gap = abs((dt.date.fromisoformat(distinct[0]) - today).days)
        if gap > RECENCY_DAYS:
            return [
                f"the new `forecast_date` {distinct[0]} must be within "
                f"{RECENCY_DAYS} day of today ({today.isoformat()})"
            ]
    return []

def append(
    previous: tuple[list[str], list[Row]],
    new: tuple[list[str], list[Row]],
) -> tuple[list[str], list[Row]]:
    """Return the hub's rows unchanged, then the new forecast's rows.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the result would fail `problems`.
    """
    pcols, prows = previous
    ncols, nrows = new
    if sorted(pcols) != sorted(ncols):
        raise ValueError(
            "the new file's columns differ from the hub's copy: "
            f"{ncols} against {pcols}"
        )
    joined = [*prows, *nrows]
    found = problems(ncols, joined, previous)
    if found:
        raise ValueError(found[0])
    return pcols, joined

    out: Path,

    checkout: Path | None = None,
    timeout: float = 30.0,
) -> bool:
    """Write the hub's file for the round to `out`, if it has one.

    The file is read from `checkout` when given (a local copy of the hub,
    used by the dry run) and from raw GitHub otherwise. Nothing is sent.
    """
    name = f"{reference_date}-{model_id}.csv"
    if checkout is not None:
        src = checkout / "model-output" / model_id / name
        if not src.exists():
            return False
        out.write_bytes(src.read_bytes())
        return True
    url = previous_url(repo, model_id, reference_date)
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=timeout) as resp:
            out.write_bytes(resp.read())
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as err:
        if err.code == 404:
            return False
        raise
    return True

def main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
    """Command line entry point."""
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    sub = p.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    f = sub.add_parser("fetch", help="Read the hub's file for the round.")
    f.add_argument("--model-id", required=True)
    f.add_argument("--reference-date", required=True)
    f.add_argument("--out", type=Path, required=True)
    f.add_argument("--repo", default=HUB_REPO)
    f.add_argument("--checkout", type=Path, default=None)
    a = sub.add_parser("append", help="Append a new forecast to that file.")
    a.add_argument("--previous", type=Path, required=True)
    a.add_argument("--new", type=Path, required=True)
    a.add_argument("--out", type=Path, required=True)
    c = sub.add_parser("check", help="Apply the hub's forecast_date rules.")
    c.add_argument("file", type=Path)
    c.add_argument("--previous", type=Path, default=None)
    c.add_argument("--today", default=None, help="YYYY-MM-DD, hub timezone.")
    args = p.parse_args(argv)
    if args.cmd == "fetch":
        found = fetch(
            args.model_id,
            args.reference_date,
            args.out,
            repo=args.repo,
            checkout=args.checkout,
        )
        print("found" if found else "absent")
        return 0
    if args.cmd == "append":
        try:
            cols, rows = append(read_rows(args.previous), read_rows(args.new))
        except ValueError as err:
            print(f"ERROR: {err}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        write_rows(args.out, cols, rows)
        print(f"Appended {args.new} to {args.previous}: {len(rows)} rows.")
        return 0
    cols, rows = read_rows(args.file)
    prev = read_rows(args.previous) if args.previous else None
    today = dt.date.fromisoformat(args.today) if args.today else None
    found_problems = problems(cols, rows, prev, today)
    for msg in found_problems:
        print(f"ERROR: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
    return 1 if found_problems else 0

Check a candidate submission file before it can be submitted.

Each check returns pass, warn, fail or skip. Only a file the hub would reject fails, which blocks the candidate; everything else is handled or warns, and is stated in the PR body. Thresholds are in policy.toml under [checks].

Format (fail): schema columns, output type, target, reference date, Saturdays, and, given tasks.json, valid locations and weeks. values no negative, NaN, infinite or unparsable values. samples exactly 100 samples per location, each a full trajectory. rt the optional wk R_t rows: quantiles at the hub's 23 levels for each location and week, finite, at least 0 and not decreasing in the level, for the weeks the round's wk R_t task takes. Skipped without such rows.

Handled (warn or pass): coverage every expected location, with every nowcast and forecast week (warns). zones health zone rows (CD-XX-NN) for every province in the file, which seabbs-rwnowcast requires (--require-zones), and each province's zones summing to it (warns only). national_sum national equals the sum of the provinces plus the unassigned cases in national.json, per sample and week (fails otherwise). A modelled province missing from the file warns. Skipped when national.json has national_source = "own": the model forecast the country itself, and the hub does not require the sum.

Plausibility (every check only warns): plausible each location's forecast near its recent data: median and 97.5% quantile under set multiples of the last 4 weeks' maximum, and the median not collapsed. bounds the 95th centile of each week is not far above the largest weekly count the location has had. growth week-on-week growth of the median over the forecast. observed the median of the last complete weeks is near what was observed.

Consistency (warn): baseline forecast median against the random walk baseline. previous shared weeks against last week's submission.

def check_rt(s: Samples, ref: str, tasks: Mapping[str, Any] | None) -> Check:
    """The `RT_TARGET` quantiles, apart from the count samples."""
    if not s.rt:
        return Check("rt", "skip", "no wk R_t rows")
    found: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    if s.rt_output_types != {"quantile"}:
        found.append(
            ("fail", f"wk R_t output types {sorted(s.rt_output_types)}")
        )
    want = sorted(RT_LEVELS)
    weeks = _rt_weeks(tasks, ref)
    for loc in sorted(s.rt):
        for week in sorted(s.rt[loc]):
            levels = s.rt[loc][week]
            where = f"{loc} {week}"
            if weeks is not None and week not in weeks:
                found.append(
                    ("fail", f"{where}: not a week of the wk R_t task")
                )
            try:
                got = sorted(float(q) for q in levels)
            except ValueError:
                found.append(("fail", f"{where}: unparsable quantile levels"))
                continue
            if got != want:
                found.append(
                    ("fail", f"{where}: {len(got)} levels, not the hub's 23")
                )
                continue
            vals = [levels[q] for q in sorted(levels, key=float)]
            if not all(math.isfinite(v) and v >= 0 for v in vals):
                found.append(
                    ("fail", f"{where}: a value is negative or not finite")
                )
            elif any(b < a for a, b in itertools.pairwise(vals)):
                found.append(("fail", f"{where}: decreases with the level"))
    n = sum(len(w) for w in s.rt.values())
    return _result("rt", found, f"wk R_t: {n} location-weeks of quantiles")

def check_schema(
    s: Samples,
    ref: str,
    file_name: str | None,
    tasks: Mapping[str, Any] | None,
) -> Check:
    """Columns, types, dates and hub task options."""
    found: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    cols = set(s.columns)
    if cols != SUBMISSION_COLUMNS:
        missing = sorted(SUBMISSION_COLUMNS - cols)
        extra = sorted(cols - SUBMISSION_COLUMNS)
        found.append(("fail", f"columns: missing {missing}, extra {extra}"))
    if s.output_types != {"sample"}:
        found.append(("fail", f"output types {sorted(s.output_types)}"))
    if TARGET not in s.targets or s.targets - {TARGET, RT_TARGET}:
        found.append(("fail", f"targets {sorted(s.targets)}"))
    if s.reference_dates != {ref}:
        found.append(
            ("fail", f"reference dates {sorted(s.reference_dates)}, not {ref}")
        )
    found.extend(_forecast_date_problems(s, ref))
    if file_name is not None and not file_name.startswith(f"{ref}-"):
        found.append(("fail", f"file name {file_name} does not start {ref}-"))
    if s.duplicates:
        found.append(("fail", f"{s.duplicates} duplicated rows"))
    weeks = {w for loc in s.locations for w in s.weeks(loc)}
    bad = sorted(w for w in weeks if not is_saturday(w))
    if bad:
        found.append(("fail", f"target end dates not Saturdays: {bad[:5]}"))
    if tasks:
        from .detect_new_vintage import open_reference_dates

        opts = _task_options(tasks)
        if ref not in open_reference_dates(tasks):
            found.append(("fail", f"{ref} is not an open reference date"))
        bad_loc = sorted(set(s.locations) - opts["location"])
        if opts["location"] and bad_loc:
            found.append(
                ("fail", f"locations not in tasks.json: {bad_loc[:5]}")
            )
        bad_w = sorted(weeks - opts["target_end_date"])
        if opts["target_end_date"] and bad_w:
            found.append(("fail", f"weeks not in tasks.json: {bad_w[:5]}"))

def check_values(s: Samples) -> Check:
    """No negative, missing or infinite values."""
    found: list[tuple[str, str]] = [
        ("fail", f"unparsable value at {u}") for u in s.unparsable
    ]
    at: set[str] = set()
    for loc in s.locations:
        vals = [v for traj in s.values[loc].values() for v in traj.values()]
        nan = sum(math.isnan(v) for v in vals)
        inf = sum(math.isinf(v) for v in vals)
        neg = sum(v < 0 for v in vals if math.isfinite(v))
        for n, what in ((nan, "NaN"), (inf, "infinite"), (neg, "negative")):
            if n:
                found.append(("fail", f"{loc}: {n} {what} values"))
                at.add(loc)
    out = _result("values", found, "all values finite and non-negative")
    if not s.unparsable:
        out.locations = sorted(at)
    return out

def check_samples(s: Samples, n: int) -> Check:
    """Exactly `n` samples per location, each covering the same weeks."""
    found: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    at: set[str] = set()
    for loc in s.locations:
        trajs = s.values[loc]
        if len(trajs) != n:
            found.append(("fail", f"{loc}: {len(trajs)} samples, not {n}"))
            at.add(loc)
        weeks = set(s.weeks(loc))
        short = [sid for sid, t in trajs.items() if set(t) != weeks]

            found.append(
                (
                    "fail",
                    f"{loc}: {len(short)} samples miss some weeks "
                    f"(e.g. sample {short[0]})",
                )

def check_national_sum(
    s: Samples, tol: float, sidecar: Mapping[str, Any]
) -> Check:
    """National equals the sum of provinces exactly, per sample and week.

    National sample k must equal the sum of province sample k plus the
    sample's modelled unassigned component (`national.json`), for every
    week, up to float noise (`tol` absolute, or 1e-12 relative). Every
    modelled province must be in the file. Skipped when the sidecar's
    `national_source` is `"own"`.
    """
    national = str(sidecar["national"])
    if sidecar.get("national_source", "sum") == "own":
        return Check(
            "national_sum",
            "skip",
            f"{national} is the model's own forecast (national.json), "
            "not the sum of the provinces",
        )
    provs = [loc for loc in s.locations if is_province(loc)]
    modelled = sorted(sidecar["modelled_provinces"])
    unassigned = _unassigned(sidecar)
    basis = f"national.json: {len(modelled)} modelled provinces" + (
        " plus the unassigned component" if unassigned else ""
    )
    found: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    missing = sorted(set(modelled) - set(s.locations))
    if missing:
        found.append(
            (
                "warn",
                f"modelled provinces missing: {missing}; national is the "
                "sum of the provinces submitted",
            )
        )
    if national not in s.values:
        found.append(("fail", f"{national} is not in the file"))
    for sid, traj in s.values.get(national, {}).items():
        for week, value in traj.items():
            parts = [s.values[p].get(sid, {}).get(week) for p in provs]
            if any(v is None for v in parts):
                found.append(
                    ("fail", f"sample {sid}, {week}: a province lacks it")
                )
                continue
            extra = unassigned.get((sid, week), 0.0)
            total = math.fsum([*(v for v in parts if v is not None), extra])
            if not math.isclose(total, value, rel_tol=1e-12, abs_tol=tol):
                found.append(
                    (
                        "fail",
                        f"sample {sid}, {week}: national {fmt(value, 12)} "
                        f"but provinces{' and unassigned' if extra else ''} "
                        f"sum to {fmt(total, 12)}",
                    )
                )
    out = _result(
        "national_sum", found, f"{national} is the exact sum ({basis})"
    )
    if out.status != "pass":
        out.summary = f"{out.summary} ({basis})"
    return out

def poisson_limits(count: float, level: float) -> tuple[float, float]:
    r"""Return the exact limits of a Poisson mean given one count.

    The lower limit $L$ has $P(X \ge k \mid L) = 1 - \text{level}$ (0
    for a count of 0) and the upper $U$ has $P(X \le k \mid U) = 1 -
    \text{level}$, so with `level` 0.975 they are the 95% interval.

    Parameters
    ----------
    count : float
        The count, rounded to the nearest whole number.
    level : float
        One-sided level, in (0.5, 1).

    Returns
    -------
    tuple of float
        `(L, U)`.
    """
    k = max(round(count), 0)
    alpha = 1.0 - level

    def solve(f: Any, lo: float, hi: float) -> float:
        while f(hi) > 0:
            hi *= 2
        for _ in range(200):
            mid = (lo + hi) / 2
            if f(mid) > 0:
                lo = mid
            else:
                hi = mid
        return (lo + hi) / 2

    upper = solve(lambda m: _poisson_cdf(k, m) - alpha, 0.0, k + 10.0)
    lower = (
        0.0
        if k == 0
        else solve(lambda m: alpha - (1 - _poisson_cdf(k - 1, m)), 0.0, k)
    )
    return lower, upper

check_plausible(s: Samples, obs: Observed, ref: date, horizon: int, c: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Check

Warn of a forecast far from the recent data, at each location.

The base is the largest of the last plausible_recent_weeks observed weeks, $m$, with the exact Poisson limits $(L, U)$ of a mean given $m$ (poisson_limits at plausible_poisson_level) in place of a fixed floor: small counts are noisy, so their limits are wide. For each week from the nowcast to the last horizon, the median must lie within plausible_median_ratio times $U$ and the 97.5% quantile within plausible_q975_ratio times $U$. The median must be at least $L$ over plausible_low_ratio where that is a case or more, unless it is at least the count already observed for that week. Locations without observed data are skipped. A breach only warns: the numbers go in the PR body for a human to read, and never rule a model out.

Source code in packages/bdbvsubmission/src/bdbvsubmission/check_forecast.py 
def check_plausible(
    s: Samples,
    obs: Observed,
    ref: dt.date,
    horizon: int,
    c: Mapping[str, Any],
) -> Check:
    """Warn of a forecast far from the recent data, at each location.

    The base is the largest of the last `plausible_recent_weeks` observed
    weeks, $m$, with the exact Poisson limits $(L, U)$ of a mean given
    $m$ (`poisson_limits` at `plausible_poisson_level`) in place of a
    fixed floor: small counts are noisy, so their limits are wide. For
    each week from the nowcast to the last horizon, the median must lie
    within `plausible_median_ratio` times $U$ and the 97.5% quantile
    within `plausible_q975_ratio` times $U$. The median must be at least
    $L$ over `plausible_low_ratio` where that is a case or more, unless
    it is at least the count already observed for that week. Locations
    without observed data are skipped. A breach only warns: the numbers
    go in the PR body for a human to read, and never rule a model out.
    """
    n_recent = int(c["plausible_recent_weeks"])
    level = float(c["plausible_poisson_level"])
    hi, tail, lo = (
        float(c["plausible_median_ratio"]),
        float(c["plausible_q975_ratio"]),
        float(c["plausible_low_ratio"]),
    )
    weeks = [_week(ref, k) for k in range(-n_recent + 1, horizon + 1)]
    found: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    for loc in s.locations:
        series = obs.counts.get(loc)
        if not series:
            continue
        recent = [series[w] for w in sorted(series)[-n_recent:]]
        top = max(recent, default=0.0)
        low, base = poisson_limits(top, level)
        least = low / lo
        for w in weeks:
            values = s.week_values(loc, w)
            if not values:
                continue
            med, q975 = quantile(values, 0.5), quantile(values, 0.975)
            if med > hi * base:
                found.append(
                    (
                        "warn",
                        f"{loc} {w}: median {fmt(med)} is over {fmt(hi)} "
                        f"times {fmt(base)}, the upper limit of the recent "
                        f"maximum {fmt(top)}",
                    )
                )
            elif q975 > tail * base:
                found.append(
                    (
                        "warn",
                        f"{loc} {w}: 97.5% quantile {fmt(q975)} is over "
                        f"{fmt(tail)} times {fmt(base)}, the upper limit of "
                        f"the recent maximum {fmt(top)}",
                    )
                )
            elif least >= 1 and med < least and med < series.get(w, math.inf):
                found.append(
                    (
                        "warn",
                        f"{loc} {w}: median {fmt(med)} is under 1/"
                        f"{fmt(lo)} of {fmt(low)}, the lower limit of the "
                        f"recent maximum {fmt(top)}",
                    )
                )
    return _result("plausible", found, "within range of the recent data")

def check_zones(s: Samples, require: bool, tol: float) -> Check:
    """Every province has zone rows, and its zones add up to it."""
    provs = [loc for loc in s.locations if is_province(loc)]
    zones: dict[str, list[str]] = {p: [] for p in provs}
    for loc in s.locations:
        parent = loc.rsplit("-", 1)[0]
        if loc.count("-") == 2 and parent in zones:
            zones[parent].append(loc)
    missing = [p for p in provs if not zones[p]]
    if not any(zones.values()):
        if require:
            return Check("zones", "fail", "no health zone rows")
        return Check("zones", "skip", "no health zone rows")
    if missing:
        return Check(
            "zones",
            "fail" if require else "warn",
            f"provinces without zone rows: {', '.join(missing)}",
        )
    off = 0
    for p, zs in zones.items():
        for sid, weeks in s.values[p].items():
            for week, value in weeks.items():
                total = sum(s.values[z].get(sid, {}).get(week, 0.0) for z in zs)
                if abs(total - value) > tol:
                    off += 1
    n = sum(len(zs) for zs in zones.values())
    if off:
        return Check(
            "zones",
            "warn",
            f"{n} zones; {off} province sample-weeks differ from the sum "
            "of their zones",
        )
    return Check("zones", "pass", f"{n} zones in {len(provs)} provinces")

def run_checks(
    submission: Path,
    *,
    reference_date: str,
    observed: Observed,
    expected_locations: Sequence[str] = (),
    tasks: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    baseline: Path | None = None,
    previous: Path | None = None,
    kind: str = "main",
    settings: Mapping[str, Any],
    national_sidecar: Mapping[str, Any],
    require_zones: bool = False,
) -> list[Check]:
    """Run every check on one candidate file."""
    s = read_samples(submission)
    ref = dt.date.fromisoformat(reference_date)
    off = float(settings["ratio_offset"])
    horizon = int(settings["horizon_weeks"])
    forecast_weeks = {_week(ref, k) for k in range(1, horizon + 1)}
    out = [
        check_schema(s, reference_date, submission.name, tasks),
        check_values(s),
        check_rt(s, reference_date, tasks),
        check_samples(s, int(settings["samples"])),
        check_coverage(
            s, ref, expected_locations, horizon, int(settings["nowcast_weeks"])
        ),
        check_zones(s, require_zones, float(settings["sum_tolerance"])),
        check_national_sum(
            s, float(settings["sum_tolerance"]), national_sidecar
        ),
        check_bounds(
            s,
            observed,
            float(settings["bound_floor"]),
            float(settings["bound_warn"]),
        ),
        check_plausible(s, observed, ref, horizon, settings),
        check_growth(
            s,
            ref,
            horizon,
            off,
            float(settings["growth_warn"]),
        ),
        check_observed(
            s,
            observed,
            int(settings["complete_lag_weeks"]),
            int(settings["complete_weeks"]),
            off,
            float(settings["observed_warn"]),
        ),
    ]
    if kind == "randomwalk":
        out.append(Check("baseline", "skip", "this is the baseline"))
    else:
        out.append(
            check_against(
                "baseline",
                s,
                read_samples(baseline)
                if baseline and baseline.exists()
                else None,
                lambda loc: sorted(
                    w for w in s.weeks(loc) if w in forecast_weeks
                ),
                off,
                float(settings["baseline_warn"]),
                "random walk baseline",
            )
        )
    out.append(
        check_against(
            "previous",
            s,
            read_samples(previous) if previous and previous.exists() else None,
            s.weeks,
            off,
            float(settings["previous_warn"]),
            "last week's submission",
        )
    )
    return out

def assess(data: Mapping[str, Any] | None, error: str = "") -> Coherence:
    """Judge one `coherence.json` payload."""
    if error:
        return Coherence("warn", f"coherence.json could not be read: {error}")
    if data is None:
        return Coherence(
            "skip", "no coherence.json, so the data were not checked"
        )
    national = str(data.get("national", "CD"))
    streams = {k: dict(v) for k, v in (data.get("streams") or {}).items() if v}
    rows = [dict(r) for r in data.get("rows") or []]
    out = Coherence(
        "pass",
        f"national ({national}) equals the sum of the provinces in every week",
        as_of=str(data.get("as_of", "")),
        national=national,
        streams=streams,
        rows=rows,
        handling=str(data.get("handling", "")),
    )
    gapped = {st: v for st, v in streams.items() if v.get("weeks_with_gap", 0)}
    if not (rows or gapped or data.get("coherent") is False):
        return out
    out.gap = True
    out.status = "fail"
    st = "total" if "total" in gapped else next(iter(gapped), "")
    if st:
        v = gapped[st]
        n = int(v["weeks_with_gap"])

docs.title: bdbvsubmission.check_ppc
docs.text:
Gate a fit on its posterior predictive checks (ppc.json).

The fit writes ppc.json beside diagnostics.json (see INTEGRATION.md): one row per location, stream and in-sample onset week with the observed count, the predictive median, central intervals and the randomised PIT. This check reports, for the gated stream (total by default) and each other stream:

  • the share of observed counts inside the 50% and 90% intervals, overall, by province, and over the last complete weeks;
  • a PIT summary: the Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance from uniform, the share in the outer deciles (0.2 when calibrated; more means the intervals are too narrow, less too wide) and the mean PIT (below 0.5 means the model predicts too high, above too low).

Thresholds are in policy.toml under [ppc]:

  • warn when the coverage of the level interval (0.9), overall or over the last recent_weeks complete weeks, is below coverage_warn (and is called poor below coverage_fail), when the PIT KS distance is above pit_ks_warn with at least pit_min_rows rows, or when a sampled fit has no readable ppc.json;
  • n/a (skip) when the model has no posterior (available: false, or no sampler and no file).

These checks are reported only. They never rule a candidate out or trigger a fallback: model choice comes from the backtest, not from one run's checks.

def coverage(rows: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]], pct: int) -> float:
    """Share of observed counts inside the `pct`% interval."""
    hits = []
    for r in rows:
        y = finite(r.get("observed"))
        lo, hi = finite(r.get(f"lower_{pct}")), finite(r.get(f"upper_{pct}"))
        if not any(math.isnan(v) for v in (y, lo, hi)):
            hits.append(lo <= y <= hi)
    return sum(hits) / len(hits) if hits else math.nan

def pit_summary(pits: Sequence[Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """KS distance from uniform, outer-decile share, mean and shape."""
    u = sorted(p for p in (finite(x) for x in pits) if not math.isnan(p))
    n = len(u)
    if not n:
        return {"n": 0, "ks": None, "outer": None, "mean": None, "shape": ""}
    ks = max(max((i + 1) / n - x, x - i / n) for i, x in enumerate(u))
    outer = sum(x < 0.1 or x > 0.9 for x in u) / n
    mean = sum(u) / n
    shape = []
    if outer > OUTER_NARROW:
        shape.append("intervals look too narrow (PIT piled at 0 and 1)")
    elif outer < OUTER_WIDE:
        shape.append("intervals look too wide (PIT bunched in the middle)")
    if mean < 0.5 - MEAN_BIAS:
        shape.append("predictions look too high (PIT mostly low)")
    elif mean > 0.5 + MEAN_BIAS:
        shape.append("predictions look too low (PIT mostly high)")
    return {
        "n": n,
        "ks": ks,
        "outer": outer,
        "mean": mean,
        "shape": "; ".join(shape),
    }

def check_ppc(
    fit_id: str,
    ppc: Mapping[str, Any] | None,
    lim: Mapping[str, Any],
    *,
    sampled: bool = True,
    error: str = "",
) -> PPCCheck:
    """Gate one fit's `ppc.json` payload."""
    if ppc is None or error:
        if not sampled and not error:
            return PPCCheck(fit_id, "skip", False, "the model has no sampler")
        why = error or "no ppc.json was written"
        return PPCCheck(
            fit_id,
            "warn",
            False,
            why,
            warnings=[f"{why}, so the fit's predictions were not checked"],
        )
    if not ppc.get("available"):
        return PPCCheck(
            fit_id,
            "skip",
            False,
            str(ppc.get("reason", "not available")),
            model=str(ppc.get("model", "")),
            config=str(ppc.get("config", "")),
        )
    rows = [
        {**r, "complete": bool(r.get("complete"))}
        for r in ppc.get("rows") or []
    ]
    levels = sorted({_pct(x) for x in ppc.get("intervals") or (0.5, 0.9)})
    present = [s for s in STREAMS if any(r["stream"] == s for r in rows)]
    present += sorted({str(r["stream"]) for r in rows} - set(present))
    stream = str(lim["stream"])
    gated = (
        [r for r in rows if r["stream"] == stream]
        if stream in present
        else rows
    )
    if stream not in present:
        stream = "all streams"
    done = sorted({r["target_end_date"] for r in gated if r["complete"]})
    recent = done[-int(lim["recent_weeks"]) :]
    out = PPCCheck(
        fit_id,
        "pass",
        True,
        model=str(ppc.get("model", "")),
        config=str(ppc.get("config", "")),
        stream=stream,
        levels=levels,
        recent_weeks=recent,
    )
    rset = set(recent)
    out.streams = {
        s: _metrics([r for r in rows if r["stream"] == s], rset, levels)
        for s in present
    }
    for loc in sorted({str(r["location"]) for r in gated}):
        lrows = [r for r in gated if r["location"] == loc]
        out.locations.append({"location": loc, **_metrics(lrows, rset, levels)})
    out.pit = pit_summary([r.get("pit") for r in gated])
    if not rows:
        out.status = "warn"
        out.warnings.append("ppc.json is available but has no rows")
        return out
    pct = _pct(lim["level"])
    head = _metrics(gated, rset, [*levels, pct])
    for key, where in (
        (f"cov{pct}", "overall"),
        (f"recent_cov{pct}", (f"over the last {len(recent)} complete weeks")),
    ):
        value = head[key]
        if math.isnan(value):
            continue
        msg = f"{pct}% interval coverage of {stream} {where} is {fmt(value)}"
        if value < lim["coverage_fail"]:
            out.warnings.append(
                f"{msg}, poor (below {fmt(lim['coverage_fail'])})"
            )
        elif value < lim["coverage_warn"]:
            out.warnings.append(
                f"{msg}, below the warning threshold "
                f"{fmt(lim['coverage_warn'])}"
            )
    ks = out.pit.get("ks")
    if (
        ks is not None
        and out.pit["n"] >= lim["pit_min_rows"]
        and ks > lim["pit_ks_warn"]
    ):
        shape = f": {out.pit['shape']}" if out.pit["shape"] else ""
        out.warnings.append(
            f"PIT of {stream} is {fmt(ks)} from uniform (KS distance), "
            f"above {fmt(lim['pit_ks_warn'])}{shape}"
        )
    out.status = "warn" if out.warnings else "pass"
    return out

                    for r in c.locations

def is_sampled(kind: str, diagnostics: Path | None) -> bool:
    """Whether the candidate's fit used a sampler.

    Random walk and fits whose diagnostics say `sampler: none` did not.
    Any other fit is taken to be sampled, so a fit that wrote nothing
    cannot pass by omission.

    if kind in UNFITTED:
        return False
    if diagnostics is None or not diagnostics.exists():
        return True
    try:
        diag = read_json(diagnostics)
    except ValueError:
        return True
    return not (isinstance(diag, dict) and diag.get("sampler") == "none")

def headline(diag: Mapping[str, Any]) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Worst R-hat, smallest ESS, divergences and draws."""
    params = diag.get("parameters", [])
    rhats = [r for p in params if not math.isnan(r := finite(p.get("rhat")))]
    bulk = [e for p in params if not math.isnan(e := finite(p.get("ess_bulk")))]
    tail = [e for p in params if not math.isnan(e := finite(p.get("ess_tail")))]
    chains = diag.get("chains", [])
    div = sum(int(c.get("divergences", 0)) for c in chains)
    draws = sum(int(c.get("draws", 0)) for c in chains) or int(
        diag.get("num_chains", 0)
    ) * int(diag.get("num_samples", 0))
    return {
        "max_rhat": max(rhats) if rhats else math.nan,
        "min_ess_bulk": min(bulk) if bulk else math.nan,
        "min_ess_tail": min(tail) if tail else math.nan,
        "n_divergent": float(div),
        "n_draws": float(draws),
        "divergent_fraction": div / draws if draws else math.nan,
    }

def verdict(
    head: Mapping[str, float], limits: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, float]]
) -> tuple[str, list[str], list[str]]:
    """Status and messages for the headline diagnostics.

    Past the *fail* threshold the fit is ruled out (`fail`). Past the
    *warn* threshold it is a `warn` only.
    """
    checks = (
        ("max R-hat", head["max_rhat"], "rhat", True),
        ("min bulk ESS", head["min_ess_bulk"], "ess_bulk", False),
        ("min tail ESS", head["min_ess_tail"], "ess_tail", False),
        (
            "divergent fraction",
            head["divergent_fraction"],
            "divergent_fraction",
            True,
        ),
    )
    failures: list[str] = []
    warnings: list[str] = []
    for name, value, key, higher_is_worse in checks:
        if math.isnan(value):
            continue

        def breaches(
            limit: float, v: float = value, hi: bool = higher_is_worse
        ) -> bool:
            return v > limit if hi else v < limit

        if breaches(limits["fail"][key]):
            failures.append(
                f"{name} is {fmt(value)}, past the failure threshold "
                f"{fmt(limits['fail'][key])}"
            )
        elif breaches(limits["warn"][key]):
            warnings.append(
                f"{name} is {fmt(value)}, past the warning threshold "
                f"{fmt(limits['warn'][key])}"
            )
    status = "fail" if failures else ("warn" if warnings else "pass")
    return status, failures, warnings

    params = [
        p
        for p in diag.get("parameters", [])
        if not math.isnan(finite(p.get("rhat")))
    ]
    ranked = sorted(params, key=lambda p: finite(p.get("ess_bulk")))
    return [
        {
            "parameter": _label(p),
            "rhat": finite(p.get("rhat")),
            "ess_bulk": finite(p.get("ess_bulk")),
            "ess_tail": finite(p.get("ess_tail")),
        }
        for p in ranked[:n]

def families(
    diag: Mapping[str, Any], rhat_threshold: float, n: int = 10
) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Diagnostics grouped by parameter name, worst bulk ESS first."""
    groups: dict[str, list[Mapping[str, Any]]] = {}
    for p in diag.get("parameters", []):
        if not math.isnan(finite(p.get("rhat"))):
            groups.setdefault(str(p["name"]), []).append(p)
    rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for name, ps in groups.items():
        rh = [finite(p.get("rhat")) for p in ps]
        eb = [e for p in ps if not math.isnan(e := finite(p.get("ess_bulk")))]
        rows.append(
            {
                "parameter": name,
                "elements": len(ps),
                "max_rhat": max(rh),
                "min_ess_bulk": min(eb) if eb else math.nan,
                "above": sum(r > rhat_threshold for r in rh),
            }
        )
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: float(r["min_ess_bulk"]))
    return rows[:n]

def check_fit(
    fit_id: str,
    diag: Mapping[str, Any] | None,
    limits: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, float]],
) -> FitCheck:
    """Gate one fit's diagnostics."""
    if diag is None:
        return FitCheck(
            fit_id,
            "error",
            True,
            failures=["no diagnostics file, so the fit cannot be judged"],
        )
    if diag.get("sampler", "nuts") == "none":
        return FitCheck(fit_id, "skip", False)
    head = headline(diag)
    status, failures, warnings = verdict(head, limits)
    out = FitCheck(
        fit_id,
        status,
        True,
        headline=head,
        failures=failures,
        warnings=warnings,
        chains=list(diag.get("chains", [])),
        bvd=diag.get("bvd"),
    )
    if status != "pass":
        out.worst = worst_parameters(diag)
        out.families = families(diag, limits["warn"]["rhat"])
    return out

def markdown(
    checks: Sequence[FitCheck],
    limits: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, float]],
    *,
    marker: str = MARKER,
    context: str = "",
) -> str:
    """The convergence report for one or more fits."""
    lines = [marker] if marker else []
    lines.append("## Fit convergence\n")
    if context:
        lines.append(context + "\n")
    rows = []
    for c in checks:
        h = c.headline
        rows.append(
            [
                f"`{c.id}`",
                STATUS_LABEL[c.status],
                fmt_rhat(h.get("max_rhat")),
                fmt(h.get("min_ess_bulk")),
                fmt(h.get("min_ess_tail")),
                fmt(h.get("n_divergent")),
                fmt(h.get("n_draws")),
            ]
        )
    lines.append(
        markdown_table(
            [
                "fit",
                "status",
                "max R-hat",
                "min ESS bulk",
                "min ESS tail",
                "divergences",
                "draws",
            ],
            rows,
        )
    )
    lines.append("")
    for c in checks:
        lines.append(f"- `{c.id}` {_PHRASE[c.status]}.")
    lines.append("")
    if any(c.chains for c in checks):
        lines.append("<details><summary>Sampler behaviour by chain</summary>\n")
        for c in checks:
            if not c.chains:
                continue
            lines.append(f"`{c.id}`:\n")
            lines.append(
                markdown_table(
                    [
                        "chain",
                        "divergences",
                        "step size",
                        "at max tree depth",
                        "mean acceptance",
                        "E-BFMI",
                    ],
                    [
                        [
                            str(ch.get("chain", "")),
                            str(ch.get("divergences", 0)),
                            fmt(finite(ch.get("step_size"))),
                            str(ch.get("tree_depth_hits", "n/a")),
                            fmt(finite(ch.get("mean_accept"))),
                            fmt(finite(ch.get("ebfmi"))),
                        ]
                        for ch in c.chains
                    ],
                )
            )
            lines.append("")
        lines.append("</details>\n")
    for c in checks:
        if not (c.failures or c.warnings):
            continue
        lines.append(f"### `{c.id}`: {STATUS_LABEL[c.status]}\n")
        lines.extend(f"- **fail**: {m}" for m in c.failures)
        lines.extend(f"- warn: {m}" for m in c.warnings)
        lines.append("")
        if c.worst:
            lines.append(
                f"<details><summary>Worst-mixing parameters of `{c.id}`"
                "</summary>\n"
            )
            lines.append(
                markdown_table(
                    ["parameter", "R-hat", "ESS bulk", "ESS tail"],
                    [
                        [
                            str(w["parameter"]),
                            fmt_rhat(w["rhat"]),
                            fmt(w["ess_bulk"]),
                            fmt(w["ess_tail"]),
                        ]
                        for w in c.worst
                    ],
                )
            )
            lines.append("\nGrouped, one row per parameter:\n")
            lines.append(
                markdown_table(
                    [
                        "parameter",
                        "elements",
                        "max R-hat",
                        "min ESS bulk",
                        f"above {fmt(limits['warn']['rhat'])}",
                    ],
                    [
                        [
                            str(f["parameter"]),
                            str(f["elements"]),
                            fmt_rhat(f["max_rhat"]),
                            fmt(f["min_ess_bulk"]),
                            str(f["above"]),
                        ]
                        for f in c.families
                    ],
                )
            )
            lines.append("\n</details>\n")
    f, w = limits["fail"], limits["warn"]
    lines.append(
        f"Thresholds. Ruled out (fall back): R-hat above "
        f"{fmt(f['rhat'])}, bulk ESS below {fmt(f['ess_bulk'])}, tail ESS "
        f"below {fmt(f['ess_tail'])}, divergences above "
        f"{fmt(f['divergent_fraction'])} of draws. Warn: {fmt(w['rhat'])}, "
        f"{fmt(w['ess_bulk'])}, {fmt(w['ess_tail'])}, "
        f"{fmt(w['divergent_fraction'])}."
    )
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"

docs.text:
Walk the fallback chain and pick the candidate to submit.

Each candidate directory (<candidates>/<id>/) holds what its matrix job produced: fit-summary.json and ppc-summary.json (none for random walk), checks.json, run.json and the hub file under submission/. A candidate is ruled out when its fit is past the convergence failure thresholds or its file would be invalid on the hub (forecast format checks, then the hub's own rules through the --validate-cmd hook, hubValidations in CI). Plausibility (how far the forecast is from the recent data) and the posterior predictive checks are reported, never gated.

A candidate ruled out only by checks tied to some provinces (values or samples there) is kept, with those provinces and their health zones from the next candidate in the chain that passes there, national re-summed, and the merged file checked and validated again (location_fallback).

If nothing is left the round is skipped.

select writes provenance.json and provenance.md and copies the chosen files to <out>/selected/.

def assess(c: Candidate, cdir: Path) -> Attempt:
    """Combine a candidate's fit gate and forecast checks."""
    a = Attempt(c.id, c.kind, c.label)
    if not cdir.is_dir():
        a.status = "missing"
        a.reasons.append("no output (the job did not run or did not finish)")
        return a
    statuses = []
    fit_path = cdir / "fit-summary.json"
    if c.kind in UNFITTED and not fit_path.exists():
        a.fit = "skip"
    elif fit_path.exists():
        fit = read_json(fit_path)
        a.fit = fit["status"]
        a.reasons += [f"convergence: {m}" for m in fit.get("failures", [])]
        a.warnings += [f"convergence: {m}" for m in fit.get("warnings", [])]
    else:
        a.fit = "error"
        a.reasons.append("convergence: no diagnostics were written")
    statuses.append(a.fit)
    ppc_path = cdir / "ppc-summary.json"
    if ppc_path.exists():
        ppc = read_json(ppc_path)
        a.ppc = ppc["status"]
        a.warnings += [
            f"ppc: {m}"
            for m in [*ppc.get("failures", []), *ppc.get("warnings", [])]
        ]
    elif c.kind in UNFITTED or a.fit == "skip":
        a.ppc = "skip"
    else:
        a.ppc = "warn"
        a.warnings.append("ppc: no posterior predictive check was written")
    # Reported only: the predictive checks never rule a candidate out.
    statuses.append("warn" if blocks(a.ppc) else a.ppc)
    checks_path = cdir / "checks.json"
    if checks_path.exists():
        checks = read_json(checks_path)
        a.checks = checks["status"]
        for ch in checks["checks"]:
            if blocks(ch["status"]):
                a.reasons.append(f"{ch['name']}: {ch['summary']}")
            elif ch["status"] == "warn":
                a.warnings.append(f"{ch['name']}: {ch['summary']}")
    else:
        a.checks = "error"
        a.reasons.append("forecast checks: no result was written")
    statuses.append(a.checks)
    notes = cdir / "submission" / "handled.json"
    if notes.exists():
        with contextlib.suppress(ValueError):
            a.handled = [str(h) for h in read_json(notes)]
    if _submission(cdir) is None:
        statuses.append("error")
        a.reasons.append("no submission file was written")
    a.status = worst(statuses)
    return a

def command_validator(template: str) -> Validator:
    """Validator running a shell command with `{submission}` filled in.

    The command's output goes to the log; exit 0 is a pass.

    def run(submission: Path, log: Path) -> str:

def select(
    policy: Policy,
    root: Path,
    validate: Validator | None,
    out: Path | None = None,
    tasks: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> tuple[Attempt | None, list[Attempt]]:
    """Return the chosen attempt (or None) and every attempt.

    With `out`, a candidate ruled out only by checks at some provinces is
    kept with those provinces from later candidates (`location_fallback`).
    """
    attempts: list[Attempt] = []
    chosen: Attempt | None = None
    chain = policy.chain()
    for i, c in enumerate(chain):
        if chosen is not None:
            attempts.append(Attempt(c.id, c.kind, c.label, status="not needed"))
            continue
        a = assess(c, root / c.id)
        attempts.append(a)
        if blocks_status(a.status):
            if out is not None and _keep_at_locations(
                a, root / c.id, chain[i + 1 :], root, out, policy, validate,
                tasks,
            ):  # fmt: skip
                chosen = a
            continue
        if not _validate(a, root / c.id, validate):
            continue
        chosen = a
    return chosen, attempts

def run_select(
    policy: Policy,
    root: Path,
    out: Path,
    validate: Validator | None,
    shadows: bool = True,
    only: bool = False,
    tasks: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Select, write provenance and copy the chosen files.

    `shadows=False` leaves the shadow candidates out, for a hub model of
    its own whose run fits none of them. `only` marks a chain of one model
    with no fallback, so a skip says so.
    """
    chosen, attempts = select(policy, root, validate, out, tasks)
    prov: dict[str, Any] = {
        "selected": chosen.id if chosen else None,
        "kind": chosen.kind if chosen else None,
        "produced_by": chosen.label if chosen else "nothing (round skipped)",
        "status": (
            ("warn" if chosen.warnings or chosen.status == "warn" else "pass")
            if chosen
            else "skip"
        ),
        "reason": _reason(chosen, attempts, only),
        "warnings": chosen.warnings if chosen else [],
        "handled": chosen.handled if chosen else [],
        "locations_substituted": chosen.substituted if chosen else {},
        "attempts": [asdict(a) for a in attempts],
        "shadows": _shadows(policy, root) if shadows else [],
    }
    if chosen:
        cdir = root / chosen.id
        run_json = cdir / "run.json"
        if run_json.exists():
            prov["run"] = read_json(run_json)
        dest = out / "selected"
        if dest.exists():
            shutil.rmtree(dest)
        shutil.copytree(Path(chosen.source) if chosen.source else cdir, dest)
    write_json(out / "provenance.json", prov)
    md = provenance_markdown(prov)
    write_text(out / "provenance.md", md)
    append_summary(md)
    return prov

    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    p.add_argument("--policy", type=Path, required=True)
    p.add_argument("--candidates", type=Path, required=True)
    p.add_argument("--model", default="", help="The chosen model")
    p.add_argument(

    p.add_argument("--out", type=Path, required=True)
    p.add_argument("--validate-cmd", default="")

    validate = (

    )
    prov = run_select(
        policy,
        args.candidates,
        args.out,

        shadows=not args.no_shadows,
        only=only,
        tasks=read_json(args.tasks) if args.tasks else None,
    )
    set_outputs(
        {
            "selected": prov["selected"] or "",
            "kind": prov["kind"] or "",
            "status": prov["status"],
            "produced_by": prov["produced_by"],
            "skipped": prov["selected"] is None,

    )

    return 0 if prov["selected"] else 3

def failing_provinces(checks: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]) -> set[str] | None:
    """Provinces behind every failing check, or None if any failure is
    about the whole file (or national) rather than a province."""
    out: set[str] = set()
    for ch in checks:
        if not blocks(str(ch["status"])):
            continue
        locs = ch.get("locations") or []
        if ch["name"] not in LOCATION_CHECKS or not locs:
            return None
        for loc in locs:
            p = province_of(str(loc))
            if p is None:
                return None
            out.add(p)
    return out
